title: Kansas City singers and pianists
summary: They discuss Joe Turner, Pete Johnson, Julia Lee, other Kansas City singers and pianists, and Juanita Bolo.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: Yes, well, that's a very good point about Kansas City.
There is something about that style of music that's distinctive. And I can't put it in words, though, I don't know what it was.
Well, the only thing -- there seemed to be a separate tradition, because, I mean, there was Joe Turner and Pete Johnson there, and there was that good old Julia Lee.
Yeah.
I always liked the way she treated a song. It wasn't great, but it was very communicative.
They had a terrific band, too. It didn't groove too much, but it was a swinging band like that. It didn't have much guts in it or something, I don't know. I don't know what that was.
Did you ever hear that other one, then, with Countess Johnson? She died very early, but she sang and played piano about then.
I think Jimmy Hamilton's wife was out there at the time.
Smith
Yeah, Vivian Green, I think, yeah.
No, but the one that you asked me about, I don't remember her.
Well, I've been told that she was very good, too. But there was another Johnson there, wasn't there? An Everett Johnson that played boogie-woogie and everything.
Yeah. And Juanita Bolo was around then. She's a jazz --
Who?
A girl named Juanita Bolo.
Oh, I don't know her.
She went up to -- she played with the band for the Traditional Jazz Club in Connecticut about four
years ago. She went up with Eddie Barefield and the band. She's from Kansas City.
Oh, yeah?
She worked with me a lot, and she plays the Kansas City style. She's gone back to Oklahoma. But a lot of them never did reach into the big time.
